on_devil_s_glen.blurb: Devil's Glen is a very long east-west cliff on the Niagara Escarpment in Ontario's Beaver Valley, inside the provincial park of the same name. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a solid minority of trad lines. Grades start at 5.5 and reach into the 5.14 range, but the bulk sits between 5.10 and 5.12, with a fair number of 5.7 to 5.9 climbs for warming up. Tight Canyon, Blank Canvas and the Looney Tunes Area hold the most routes. Blackflies and mosquitoes can be bad in June and July.

va_darkside.blurb: Darkside is a bouldering zone in Jaybird Gorge in southwest Virginia, on the far side of the creek from Lightside. The problems are scattered over three sectors, Lower, Center and Upper Darkside, among many boulders and a few short crags. Everything here is bouldering, with a wide spread: plenty of V0 to V2 for newcomers, a thick middle of V3 to V4, and a tail of hard problems up to V10. The boulders face mostly north, so the area sees far less sun than Lightside and takes much longer to dry after rain or snow.

bc_comox_lake.blurb: Comox Lake lies near the town of Cumberland on Vancouver Island, roughly an hour north of Nanaimo, in a scenic lakeside setting. The rock is basalt. Sport climbing is the main event, with a good number of boulder problems and a smaller helping of trad and top-rope lines. Most sport routes fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with the thickest cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, and the boulders mostly run V0 to V3. The crags are small and close together, so a day can cover several of them. Huckleberry Hill and the Sherman Boulders are among the named spots.

ca_salt_point_state_park.blurb: Salt Point sits on the Sonoma coast north of Jenner, along Highway 1, where tilted sandstone meets the Pacific. Wave and salt action has pitted the rock into honeycomb-like tafoni, and the climbing is set in beach and forest scenery. The sandstone is tougher than most around the Bay Area but still crumbly in spots, with sharp holds. Bouldering makes up about two thirds of it, mostly V0 to V5 with a few harder, alongside sport routes mainly from 5.9 to 5.12 and a few trad lines. Secrets, Call Box Rocks, Ocean Cove and Treasure Chest are the bigger zones. Weather is often cool and foggy, and tides and surf matter at some walls.

co_crags_the.blurb: The Crags cover the west face of Twin Sisters, a few miles south of Estes Park beside Highway 7 near Lily Lake. The rock is rough granite and gneiss, with plenty of knobs and edges, in an alpine-feeling forested setting with views toward Longs Peak. Sport routes outnumber trad about two to one, and the area is known for multipitch sport link-ups across several formations. Climbs run from short pitches to four pitches, nearly all between 5.8 and 5.12 with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. Lower Great Face, with the Wizard's Gate area, is the largest zone, followed by Woodstone and neighbors, Sharksfin and Rib Rock. Expect an uphill walk of roughly an hour to the main faces.

nv_juniper_canyon.blurb: Juniper Canyon is a stream-cut side canyon in Red Rocks, near Las Vegas, and a trad-heavy corner of the area. Nearly all of its climbs are trad, many of them multipitch on walls and buttresses of sandstone. Moderates are plentiful: grades cluster from 5.7 to 5.10, with a smaller number of 5.11 and 5.12 lines. Jackrabbit Buttress, Brownstone Wall, Ginger Buttress and Jungle Wall hold the most routes, while Rose Tower is good for moderate climbs and Cloud Tower and Rainbow Wall offer bigger ones. Brownstone Wall faces east and is a long hike in, taking up to two hours. The sandstone is fragile when wet, so wait for dry ground.
